today_summary: GCM26 marks $4,399 with ATM IV 22.60% and 107 DTE, putting the 1σ daily move at $62.63 (1.42%). Chain-wide P/C OI reads 0.34, but that headline is distorted by 110,430 far-OTM call contracts at $5,500 and above — inside the tradable ±25% window the ratio is a far more neutral 0.735. Today's flow is aggressively call-side: 11,172 call contracts versus 2,739 puts (P/C volume 0.25), concentrated in the $5,000 calls (1,951), $4,600 calls (1,079) and $4,800 calls (980). Net GEX within ±$200 of spot is +210.1, so dealers are long gamma locally and are dampening intraday range.
five_day_thesis: The defining change over five sessions is a 7.56% spot advance from $4,089.8 to $4,399.0 (+$309.2) that arrived with IV expanding, not compressing — ATM IV rose 21.67% → 22.60% (+0.93pp), which is the signature of demand-led buying rather than a drift higher into decaying premium. The second change is a full dealer-posture inversion: windowed net GEX flipped from −10.65 on 2026-08-04 to +79.11 on 08-05, then compounded to +294.29, +276.67 and +417.43 — a 5x build in three sessions that turned the regime from vol-amplifying to vol-suppressing. Positioning grew asymmetrically into that move, with call OI up 11,701 contracts (179,043 → 190,744) against just 4,711 added puts (60,118 → 64,829), yet P/C OI held flat at 0.34 all week because the new length landed in strikes that were already call-heavy. What has not moved is the structural skeleton: max pain has been pinned at $6,500 for five straight sessions, the put wall at $3,500 and the call wall at $8,000 have not migrated a single tick — that inertia means the $2,101 gap between spot and max pain is legacy far-dated OI, not a same-day magnet. The actionable consequence is that spot has now climbed to within $111 of the $4,510 gamma flip, so this week's regime question is whether price can clear the $4,500–$4,510 call shelf where 14,751 contracts of call OI sit stacked.

ATM IV expanded 21.67% → 22.60% (+0.93pp) while spot rallied — demand-led buying, not a low-vol drift
Call OI added 11,701 contracts vs only 4,711 puts, yet P/C OI stayed frozen at 0.34 as new length stacked into already call-heavy strikes
Gamma flip strike drifted higher across the week; the full-chain cumulative crossing now sits at $4,510, just $111 above spot
Max pain ($6,500), put wall ($3,500) and call wall ($8,000) were unchanged all 5 sessions — the far-dated skeleton is inert
prediction: Bias constructive but range-capped while spot holds above $4,300. With net GEX +210.1 inside ±$200, dealer hedging suppresses range — expect a grind inside $4,300–$4,500 rather than trend expansion, with fades favored at the extremes and the 1σ band of $62.63 containing most sessions. A sustained break above the $4,510 gamma flip flips dealers short gamma into the move and opens $4,600; loss of $4,300, where 2,344 puts sit as the nearest real floor, invalidates the constructive read and exposes the $4,000 shelf.
